::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How to include a document into another document?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/11311/how-to-include-a-document-into-another-document), asked by [RoflcoptrException](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/3316/roflcoptrexception) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-02-17; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I have two documents A and B. Both of them are separate documents. But document A also has to include document B. 
>
> Now if I use `\include{B}` i get the following error:
>
> ```latex
> ! LaTeX Error: Can be used only in preamble.
>
> See the LaTeX manual or LaTeX Companion for explanation.
> Type  H <return>  for immediate help.
>  ...                                              
>
> l.1 \documentclass
>                   [11pt]{article}
> ? 
> ```
>
> So how can I force to include document B with the "style" and "template" of document A?
:::

Cut the content (the part between `\begin{document}...\end{document}` of `B.tex` into a new file `B-content.tex`.

Change `B.tex` to be:

```latex
\documentclass{...}
% your preamble here
\begin{document}
\include{B-content}
\end{document}
```

Then put `\include{B-content}` into `A.tex`.
